**Summary of observations:**
- Test image: longitudinally split corn stalk on dark blue fabric background
- Internal pith: tan/orange-brown, shredded, fibrous with vascular bundles visible
- Small dark specks scattered throughout (characteristic sclerotia)
- Dry, disintegrated pith tissue

**Key comparison:** The Charcoal stalk rot reference bottom-right panel is nearly identical — same dark blue fabric background, same tan/orange fibrous pith texture, same small dark specks (sclerotia of *Macrophomina phaseolina*). Charcoal rot causes the pith to completely disintegrate, leaving only the fibrous vascular bundles with visible black microsclerotia embedded throughout.

Diplodia stalk rot shows whiter/more bleached tissue; Anthracnose shows black discoloration; Fusarium shows pink/salmon hues. None match the warm tan/orange + scattered dark sclerotia pattern.
